A 27-year-old G1P0 at 12 weeks estimated gestational age presents for prenatal care. The patient says she has occasional nausea and vomiting and a few episodes of palpitations and diarrhea this last week. Physical examination is unremarkable, except for a heart rate of 145/min. Basic thyroid function tests are shown in the table below. Which of the following additional laboratory tests would be most useful is assessing this patient’s condition?
Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) 
0.28 mIU/L (0.3–4.5 mIU/L)
Total T4
12 µg/dL (5.4–11.5 µg/dL)?

                    ### Question
                    A 27-year-old G1P0 at 12 weeks estimated gestational age presents for prenatal care. The patient says she has occasional nausea and vomiting and a few episodes of palpitations and diarrhea this last week. Physical examination is unremarkable, except for a heart rate of 145/min. Basic thyroid function tests are shown in the table below. Which of the following additional laboratory tests would be most useful is assessing this patient’s condition?
Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) 
0.28 mIU/L (0.3–4.5 mIU/L)
Total T4
12 µg/dL (5.4–11.5 µg/dL)?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Total triiodothyronine (T3) levels
opb. Free thyroxine (T4) levels
opc. Thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG) levels
opd. Thyroid peroxidase (TPO) antibodies
ope. Thyrotropin receptor antibodies (TRAb)

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient presents with symptoms and lab findings suggestive of hyperthyroidism, characterized by low TSH and high total T4. In pregnancy, total T4 can be elevated due to increased thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG), making free T4 a more reliable indicator of thyroid function. Therefore, assessing free T4 levels is crucial to determine if the patient has true hyperthyroidism or if the changes are due to pregnancy-related physiological alterations. Additionally, the presence of palpitations, diarrhea, and tachycardia raises the suspicion of Graves' disease, for which thyrotropin receptor antibodies (TRAb) testing would be useful. However, the immediate need is to confirm the thyroid status with free T4 levels. Thus, the most useful additional laboratory test in this context is the free thyroxine (T4) level.
